title: Founder & Full-Stack Engineer
description: Designed, built, and operate in production a subscription-based AI language-learning platform: eight independent Go microservices behind a Bun/Elysia/HTML6 web frontend, real-time voice tutoring over WebSockets, and adaptive spaced-repetition review, helping users learn German, English, Russian, and French.

accomplishments.title: Usage-Based Subscription Tiers
accomplishments.description: Designed and shipped usage-based subscription tiers (Free, Pro, Premium) for uLearn, with consistent limit enforcement across every paid feature.
accomplishments.challenge: A real paid product isn't just features that work: it's features that can be metered. Every paid tier needed usage tracked and enforced across chat, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and flashcard generation, features spanning several independent Go services instead of one codebase, so **there was no single place to just check a limit and move on**.
accomplishments.solution: Built a shared usage counter in DynamoDB that every service checks and increments before allowing a metered action, so **tier limits get enforced consistently no matter which service handles the request**. Free, Pro, and Premium tiers, billed through Lemon Squeezy, all run on the same counter rather than each service tracking its own.
results: Shipped Free, Pro, and Premium subscription tiers with usage enforced consistently across every service from one shared counter
Operate the platform solo in production with real users
Metering covers every paid feature: AI chat, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and flashcard generation

accomplishments.title: Eight Independent Go Microservices
accomplishments.description: Split uLearn's backend into eight independent Go microservices, one per external provider, deployed on AWS ECS.
accomplishments.challenge: Every new AI or data provider (Gemini-powered vocabulary generation, Gemini-powered chat and AI tutor mode, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, generated reading texts, YouTube video search, email, and core user/card data) added to a single Go web service meant more surface area in one codebase, one deploy unit, one blast radius, even before it became an actual bottleneck. **The plan was to split before it became a problem, not after.**
accomplishments.solution: Gave each provider its own independent Go service, built with the Fiber framework for speed of iteration, with the web frontend (Bun, Elysia, HTML6) just calling into whichever one it needed for a given request. **The split was for development speed, not performance.** Eight small, consistent codebases are easier to reason about solo than one growing one. Deployed all eight on AWS ECS, which handles scaling and restarts per service without needing Kubernetes, keeping solo operational overhead low despite the extra services.
results: Split uLearn into eight independent Go services (api, agent, chat, tts, stt, text, video, and email) instead of one growing web server
Kept solo operational overhead low by deploying all eight on AWS ECS, with no Kubernetes needed
Consistent Fiber-based patterns across every service made adding or debugging any one of them fast

accomplishments.title: Real-Time Voice AI Tutor
accomplishments.description: Built a real-time voice conversation pipeline for uLearn's AI tutor over WebSockets, with voice-activity detection for natural turn-taking.
accomplishments.challenge: A voice conversation with an AI tutor needed to actually feel like a conversation: knowing when a learner stopped talking without a fixed push-to-talk button, keeping round-trip latency low enough that replies didn't feel like a laggy request/response cycle, and never letting the assistant's own voice get picked back up by the mic mid-reply. **None of that is solved by just wiring speech-to-text and text-to-speech together.**
accomplishments.solution: Benchmarked WebSocket against plain HTTP for the round trip through the STT provider (Groq Whisper-large-v3) and TTS provider (gpt-4o-mini-tts), and WebSocket won on latency in both the docs and manual testing, so the whole pipeline runs over it: client to web service, and web service to each provider. Voice-activity detection (`@ricky0123/vad-web`, Silero VAD) flags when the learner stops talking, the captured audio gets sent, and **recording stays off entirely until the assistant's reply finishes playing**, so the two sides never talk over each other.
results: Real-time voice conversation with an AI tutor over WebSockets, with voice-activity detection instead of push-to-talk
Prevents the assistant's own voice from being picked up by the mic by blocking recording during playback
Contextual corrections mid-conversation as part of the same voice pipeline

title: Full-Stack Engineer
description: Built a suite of internal libraries and products from scratch: a RAG chatbot library with web scraping and vector-based retrieval, a custom HTML templating engine and expression language, and a visual site-building CMS used to ship a full e-commerce reference site.

accomplishments.title: Botty — RAG Chatbot Library
accomplishments.description: Built an npm library for creating RAG chatbots with web scraping, vector-based retrieval, and multi-model support.
accomplishments.challenge:
The library needed to **turn any company's URL into a working chatbot**: paste a domain into a demo, and the scrape → chunk → embed → retrieve pipeline behind it had to work generically, with nothing hardcoded to one site or one AI provider.

**None of that existed yet to build on.** Scraping, chunking, embedding, and retrieval all had to be designed and wired together with no prior implementation to lean on.
accomplishments.solution:
Built the pipeline end-to-end: scrape a site from its sitemap, split content into fixed-size overlapping chunks, embed them, and store the vectors in Qdrant keyed by the source URL. On each user question, embed the question the same way, pull the closest-matching chunks back out of Qdrant, and feed them to the model as context.

Generalized the scripts to run against any target domain, added an API-calling mapper so the model could trigger backend actions mid-conversation, and made the AI provider itself configurable (OpenAI or a local Ollama model) behind one interface. Shipped a lightweight demo server so the whole pipeline could be tried end-to-end from a URL.
results: Built a domain-agnostic RAG pipeline (scraping, chunking, embedding, and retrieval) usable on any company's site from just a URL, with vectors stored in Qdrant
Added AI-driven function calling for backend actions mid-conversation, and made the model itself configurable: hosted (OpenAI) or local (Ollama), behind one interface
Shipped a demo web app so the whole pipeline could be tried end-to-end from a URL

accomplishments.title: HTML6 — Custom Server-Side Templating Engine
accomplishments.description: Designed and built a from-scratch HTML templating and rendering engine, evolved from an earlier internal library (@nodedk/html) into HTML6, used as the rendering layer for SanityCMS and Nobo.
accomplishments.challenge:
HTML6 is a Node.js engine that compiles JavaScript templates into HTML for server-side rendering. The goal wasn't just correctness; **it had to be the fastest engine of its kind.**

The first version resolved conditionals, loops, and slots with nested O(n) scans, and it failed benchmarks as templates grew. The brief also ruled out feature creep: the fix had to be a faster architecture, not more features.
accomplishments.solution:
Following my manager's suggestion, rebuilt the compiler around masking/unmasking: special tags (if, else-if, else, map) get hashed into a lookup table during parsing, so the compiler works over a flat string instead of re-walking nested structures. A final pass swaps each hash back for its render function.

Kept the language minimal (conditionals, loops, and prop passing, nothing more) and **validated it in production twice over**: as the rendering layer for [Nobo](https://en.nobo.no/), the client site built at Eldøy, and as the engine behind [uLearn](https://ultimatelearning.app), my own product.
results: Replaced nested O(n) tag resolution with a masking/unmasking compile step. HTML6 is now the fastest template engine in the world
Kept the language minimal (if/else-if/else, map, prop passing) instead of adding features, and validated it in production on both Nobo and uLearn
Published as a public package on npm, with README and docs

accomplishments.title: SanityCMS — Visual Site Builder
accomplishments.description: Built a CMS layer on top of Sanity Studio that renders fully dynamic sites (headers, footers, pages, sections) using the HTML6 engine, with live visual click-to-edit editing.
accomplishments.challenge:
Sanity's click-to-edit and live-preview tooling is built primarily for Next.js frontends, with tight framework-level hooks into Studio.

This stack was different: HTML6 for server-side rendering, vanilla JS on the client, plain Node.js underneath. Nothing Next.js provided a path for, and linking Studio's preview to the actual rendered page meant **there was no ready integration to reach for.**
accomplishments.solution:
Reverse-engineered Sanity's preview flow to understand what it expected, then **built a token-based handoff in its place**: Studio issues a token, the frontend exchanges it for draft-content access, and edits show up on the live page in real time. Moving those tokens safely between the app and Studio meant extending Eldøy's own cookie-management library, since it wasn't built for that exchange either.

On top of that, modeled pages and sections dynamically instead of hardcoding one schema per page, wired up automatic main-layout assignment so editors didn't have to set it by hand, and built a custom sanity-plugin-markdown with autocompletion, sanitization, and full-screen editing for content authors.
results: Built a custom token-based preview integration since Sanity's tooling assumes Next.js, so editors get real-time click-to-edit on a plain HTML6/Node.js stack
Site fully data-driven, with pages, sections, and layouts assembled dynamically from Sanity content
Custom markdown plugin with autocompletion, sanitization, and full-screen editing shipped for content authors

accomplishments.title: Nobo — E-Commerce Reference Site
accomplishments.description: Built designo-nobo, a full e-commerce reference implementation on top of SanityCMS and HTML6, covering search, product listing and detail, and category pages.
accomplishments.challenge:
**Nobo was already a real, live e-commerce site**, running on Mustache, with click-to-edit wired in the same way it had already been built for SanityCMS. Migrating its entire template layer to HTML6 without breaking production was the actual stress test for the engine, not a synthetic benchmark.

On top of the migration, product data (variants, pricing, category structure) had to render correctly across search, listings, product detail, and category pages, and the shared @nodedk/sanity unwrap layer was throwing circular-reference errors whenever content referenced itself.
accomplishments.solution:
**Migrated Nobo's full template layer from Mustache to HTML6 live**, rebuilding header, footer, hero, search, product list, product detail, category, and FAQ sections against HTML6 schemas and render handlers, while keeping the site's existing click-to-edit integration working throughout.

Traced the circular-reference errors to self-referencing content in Sanity and rewrote @nodedk/sanity's unwrap logic to handle it, centralizing all data reshaping into one reusable method and shipping a new package version adopted across the site.
results: Migrated Nobo's live production storefront from Mustache to HTML6 without breaking it: the real-world proof behind HTML6's speed
Modeled product variants, pricing, and category data so it rendered correctly across search, listing, detail, and category pages
Fixed self-referencing circular-reference bugs in @nodedk/sanity's unwrap logic, centralized data reshaping into one method, and shipped the new version site-wide
